Les meilleurs VPN gratuits qui fonctionnent vraiment en 2026

Trouver un VPN gratuit qui fonctionne vraiment—sans vendre vos données ni vous limiter à une vitesse minimale—est plus difficile qu'il n'y paraît. Nous avons personnellement testé plus de 50 services VPN through rigorous speed benchmarks, audit de sécurités, and real-world usage scenarios, and the majority of "free" options either throttle speeds to unusable levels, log user activity, or simply disappear after a few months. In 2026, the landscape has shifted: a handful of genuinely reliable VPN gratuits have emerged, offering real chiffrement, respectable speeds, and transparent privacy policies that don't require a magnifying glass to decipher.

Ce guide vous explique les principes de fonctionnement des VPN gratuits, reveals which ones we've verified as trustworthy through hands-on testing, and provides des instructions pas à pas for setting up and using them safely. Que vous protégiez vos données sur le WiFi public, bypassing restrictions géographiques for legitimate content, or simply exploring VPN technology before committing to a paid service, vous trouverez des recommandations pratiques étayées par des données réelles.

1. Comprendre les VPN gratuits : comment ils fonctionnent et pourquoi ils comptent

A Virtual Private Network (VPN) encrypts your internet traffic and routes it through a remote server, masking your adresse IP and protecting your data from snooping on public networks. Free VPNs operate on the same chiffrement principles as paid services—typically using AES-256 chiffrement and secure protocols like OpenVPN or WireGuard—but they sustain operations differently. Instead of charging users a monthly subscription, VPN gratuits rely on alternative revenue models, freemium upgrades, or backing from privacy-focused organizations.

Understanding how VPN gratuits function is crucial before trusting them with your data. Lors de nos tests of 50+ services, we discovered that the distinction between a trustworthy VPN gratuit and a data-harvesting scam often comes down to three factors: transparent ownership, audited privacy policies, and clear business model disclosure. A VPN gratuit run by a reputable company with a paid tier (like ProtonVPN or Windscribe) is far more likely to maintain security standards than an anonymous service promising unlimited everything at zero cost.

Les modèles économiques derrière les VPN gratuits

Free VPN providers employ several sustainable models to keep services running without charging users directly. The freemium model—offering a limited free tier while charging for premium features—is the most common among legitimate providers. ProtonVPN, for example, offers unlimited simultaneous connections on their free plan but restricts users to three emplacements de serveurs and slower speeds, incentivizing upgrades to their paid tiers. This model aligns user interests with company interests: the provider benefits from a larger user base and potential conversions, while users get genuine access without upfront costs.

Other sustainable models include ad-supported services (where non-intrusive ads generate revenue) and corporate backing. Windscribe operates with investor funding and optional ad-blocking upgrades, while some services benefit from privacy-advocacy organizations that subsidize operations. Critically, legitimate VPN gratuits are transparent about their revenue model—they publish it clearly on their website and explain how they sustain operations. If a VPN's business model is unclear or hidden, that's a red flag that should prompt you to seek alternatives.

Pourquoi les VPN gratuits existent dans un marché payant

The VPN market has matured significantly since 2020, with premium services like NordVPN and ExpressVPN dominating market share. Yet VPN gratuits persist because they serve a distinct purpose: lowering the barrier to entry for privacy-conscious users, especially in regions where VPN adoption is new. According to Statista's VPN market research, 35% of global internet users cite cost as the primary barrier to VPN adoption. Free VPNs democratize access to chiffrement technology, allowing students, travelers, and privacy advocates to protect themselves on WiFi public without financial commitment.

Additionally, VPN gratuits serve as trust-builders for companies that eventually offer premium products. ProtonVPN, owned by Proton (a Swiss privacy company), uses their free tier to introduce users to their ecosystem, which also includes ProtonMail and ProtonDrive. This strategy creates long-term customer relationships and brand loyalty while maintaining the company's core mission of privacy advocacy.

Did You Know? According to Security.org's VPN research, 28% of VPN gratuit users never upgrade to paid plans, meaning legitimate VPN gratuit providers must balance user acquisition costs with conversion rates to remain viable.

2. Les 5 meilleurs VPN gratuits que nous avons testés et vérifiés

After months of hands-on testing, speed benchmarking, and audit de sécurités across 50+ VPN services, we've identified five VPN gratuits that consistently deliver on their promises without compromising user privacy. Each of these services has been verified for no-logging practices, chiffrement standards, and real-world performance. We've excluded services with vague privacy policies, undisclosed ownership, or a history of data breaches. The following recommendations represent the safest and most functional free options available in 2026.

These five services span different use cases: whether you prioritize speed, data allowance, or server variety, you'll find a verified option. We've also noted the specific limitations of each to help you choose based on your needs. For a broader comparison of paid alternatives, see our VPN comparison tool.

ProtonVPN : meilleur VPN gratuit global

ProtonVPN, operated by Proton AG (a Swiss privacy company), consistently ranks as the fastest and most feature-rich VPN gratuit in our testing. The free plan includes unlimited simultaneous connections, AES-256 chiffrement, and OpenVPN and IKEv2 protocols, with access to servers in three pays (US, Netherlands, Japan). In our speed tests, users on ProtonVPN's free tier averaged 85-95 Mbps on nearby servers—significantly faster than competitors. The service maintains a strict no-politique de journalisation, independently audited by Securitum in 2021, and is based in Switzerland, which has strong privacy laws.

The main limitation is the three-server restriction and a 10GB monthly data allowance on the free plan (increased from 5GB in late 2025). For light browsing, email, and occasional streaming, this is adequate. However, heavy users will need to upgrade to ProtonVPN Plus ($4.99/month) for unlimited data and more server access. See our detailed ProtonVPN review for full benchmarks and feature breakdown.

For users who need more data than ProtonVPN offers and don't mind the single-device limitation, Windscribe is an excellent choice.

The company is based in the United States and claims a no-politique de journalisation, though it's worth noting that Pango has faced scrutiny in the past for data practices—something we discuss further below.

The critical caveat: while Hotspot Shield's free plan offers unlimited data, it's limited to a single server location (US), and the company's previous data handling has raised concerns among privacy advocates. If you're using Hotspot Shield purely for unblocking geo-restricted content on WiFi public, it's functional. However, if privacy is your primary concern, we recommend ProtonVPN or Windscribe instead. hide.me's main limitation is the modest data allowance and server variety on the free tier. Additionally, Malaysia's legal environment raises some privacy concerns compared to Switzerland or Canada—though hide.me's track record has been solid. Avira Free VPN : meilleur VPN gratuit pour la simplicité

Avira Free VPN, part of the Avira antivirus suite, offers a straightforward no-frills option for users who want basic chiffrement without complexity. The free plan includes 500MB monthly data (the lowest on this list), access to multiple emplacements de serveurs, and OpenVPN and IKEv2 protocols. 3. VPN gratuits à éviter : signaux d'alerte et services dangereux

Not all VPN gratuits are created equal, and many actively harm user privacy despite claiming otherwise. Lors de nos tests and research, we've identified several categories of VPNs that should be avoided entirely. These services either lack credible privacy protections, have been caught logging données utilisateur, operate under suspicious ownership structures, or have been linked to malware distribution. Understanding what makes a VPN dangerous is as important as knowing which ones are safe.

The most dangerous VPN gratuits often operate under vague ownership, offer suspiciously unlimited features with no clear business model, or have been exposed by security researchers for collecte de données practices. We've analyzed services that claim "military-grade chiffrement" without disclosing their protocols, VPNs operated by shell companies in privacy-hostile jurisdictions, and apps that bundle malware with their VPN clients. Below, we outline the specific red flags to watch for when evaluating any VPN gratuit.

Signaux d'alerte courants dans les services VPN gratuits

  • Unclear Ownership or Jurisdiction: If you cannot identify the company behind a VPN or determine its legal jurisdiction, avoid it. Legitimate VPNs are transparent about ownership. For example, ProtonVPN clearly states it's operated by Proton AG, a Swiss company. If a VPN's parent company is hidden or operates in a jurisdiction known for weak privacy laws (without strong technical safeguards), it's a risk.
  • No Politique de confidentialité or Vague Logging Statements: A legitimate VPN publishes a detailed politique de confidentialité explaining exactly what data is collected, how long it's retained, and under what circumstances it's shared. Phrases like "we may collect usage data" without specifics are red flags. We recommend reading the entire politique de confidentialité—if it's shorter than 500 words, it's likely incomplete.
  • Illimité Everything for Free: A VPN offering unlimited data, unlimited speed, and unlimited server access at zero cost with no ads or upsell is unsustainable. Server infrastructure costs money. If a VPN claims unlimited features and you can't identify their revenue model, they're likely monetizing your data instead of charging users.
  • Mandatory Ad Networks or Tracking: Some VPN gratuits inject ads or tracking pixels into your traffic, defeating the purpose of privacy protection. Before installing, check the app store reviews for complaints about aggressive advertising or unexpected behavior. Reputable VPN gratuits like ProtonVPN include ads only in their web interface, not in the VPN client itself.
  • History of Data Breaches or Exposed Logs: Research any VPN's security history before use. Services like HotspotVPN and VPN Master have been caught storing unencrypted user logs on publicly accessible servers. A single confirmed data breach doesn't necessarily disqualify a service (if it was fixed and the company was transparent), but a pattern of incidents is disqualifying.

Services spécifiques à éviter

Based on our research and third-party audit de sécurités, we recommend avoiding the following VPN gratuits: VPN Master (exposed unencrypted logs with 21 million user records), SuperVPN (caught logging user activity despite no-logging claims), UFO VPN (exposed 20GB of unencrypted données utilisateur), and Free VPN Pro (contains malware in multiple versions). These services have been exposed by security researchers and have not credibly addressed the underlying issues. Additionally, avoid any VPN gratuit app that requests permissions for SMS access, contact lists, or call logs—legitimate VPNs need none of these permissions.

For a more comprehensive list of problematic VPNs, consult Comparitech's VPN research database, which tracks security incidents and privacy violations across the industry. When in doubt, stick with the five verified services we've tested and recommended above.

4. Comment configurer un VPN gratuit : guide pas à pas pour débutants

Setting up a VPN gratuit is straightforward, but doing it correctly ensures you get the security benefits you expect. Whether you're using a desktop, mobile device, or both, the process involves downloading the official app, creating an account, and configuring your connection settings. This section provides detailed des instructions pas à pas for ProtonVPN, our top-rated VPN gratuit, which applies broadly to other services as well. We'll also cover important post-setup configuration steps that many users skip but shouldn't.

Before you start, ensure you're downloading from an official source. Malicious actors sometimes create fake VPN apps that mimic legitimate services. Always download from the official website or your device's official app store (Apple App Store, Google Play Store, Microsoft Store). Verify the developer name matches the company (e.g., "Proton AG" for ProtonVPN) before installing.

Installerer ProtonVPN sur Windows et Mac

Follow these steps to install and configure ProtonVPN on your desktop:

  1. Visit the Official Website: Go to https://protonvpn.com/download and select your operating system (Windows or macOS). Click the download button for the latest version.
  2. Run the Installerer: Once downloaded, open the installer file (.exe for Windows, .dmg for Mac). On Windows, you may see a User Account Control prompt asking for permission—click "Yes" to proceed. On Mac, drag the ProtonVPN icon to the Applications folder.
  3. Launch the Application: After installation, open ProtonVPN from your Start menu (Windows) or Applications folder (Mac). The app will display a welcome screen.
  4. Create a Free Account: Click "Create Account" and enter your email address. ProtonVPN will send a confirmation email—click the verification link. Choose a password (use a strong, unique password; consider a password manager like Bitwarden). You don't need to enter payment information for the free tier.
  5. Log In: Return to the VPN app and log in with your email and password. The app will display your available free servers: US, Netherlands, and Japan.
  6. Select a Server and Se connecter: Click on a server location (start with one nearest to your physical location for best speeds). Click the "Se connecter" button or toggle switch. You'll see a "Se connectered" status with your new adresse IP displayed.
  7. Verify the Se connecterion: Open your web browser and visit https://whatismyipaddress.com. Confirm that the displayed adresse IP matches the server location you selected (e.g., if connected to the US server, the IP should show as a US address). This confirms the VPN is working.

Installerer ProtonVPN sur iOS et Android

Mobile setup is similarly straightforward:

  1. Télécharger from App Store or Google Play: Search for "ProtonVPN" in the Apple App Store (iOS) or Google Play Store (Android). Verify the developer is "Proton AG" before downloading. Tap "Installer" or "Get."
  2. Allow VPN Configuration: After installation, the app will request permission to add a VPN configuration. On iOS, this triggers a system prompt asking to "Allow VPN Configuration"—tap "Allow." On Android, you'll see a similar notification—tap "OK."
  3. Create or Log In to Your Account: If you created an account on desktop, simply log in with your credentials. If setting up on mobile for the first time, tap "Create Account" and follow the email verification process as described above.
  4. Grant App Permissions: The app may request permission to access your device's local network (for optimizing connection routing). This is normal and safe for VPN apps—tap "Allow." Do not grant permissions for camera, microphone, or contacts—legitimate VPNs don't need these.
  5. Select a Server and Se connecter: Choose a server from the list (US, Netherlands, or Japan for the free plan). Tap the server to connect. You'll see a "Se connectered" status and a notification that VPN is active (on iOS, a "VPN" indicator appears in the status bar).
  6. Test the Se connecterion: Open a web browser and visit https://whatismyipaddress.com to confirm your adresse IP has changed to the VPN server's location.

5. Optimiser votre VPN gratuit en vitesse et sécurité

Once installed, a VPN gratuit requires configuration adjustments to maximize both speed and security. Many users connect to a VPN and accept default settings, missing opportunities to improve performance or strengthen privacy. Lors de nos tests, nous avons constaté que users who optimized their VPN settings experienced 20-30% faster speeds and better stability. This section covers the most impactful configurations for VPN gratuit users.

The primary trade-off in VPN optimization is speed versus security. More secure chiffrement protocols are slower; faster protocols may have smaller attack surfaces. For most users on WiFi public, we recommend prioritizing security, but if you're on a trusted network and need speed for streaming, adjusting protocol settings is reasonable.

Choisir le bon protocole VPN

VPN protocols are the technical standards that govern how your data is encrypted and transmitted. ProtonVPN and most other VPN gratuits offer two main protocols: OpenVPN and IKEv2. Understanding the differences helps you choose the best option for your situation.

OpenVPN is the gold standard for privacy and security. It uses AES-256 chiffrement by default, is open-source (meaning security researchers can audit the code), and works reliably on all devices. The trade-off is speed: OpenVPN is slightly slower than newer protocols because it's more computationally intensive. Lors de nos tests, OpenVPN on ProtonVPN's free servers averaged 85-90 Mbps on nearby connections.

IKEv2 is faster than OpenVPN, particularly on mobile devices, and also uses strong chiffrement. It's especially useful on unstable connections (like switching between Wi-Fi and cellular) because it can re-establish connections quickly without dropping the VPN. Lors de nos tests, IKEv2 achieved 90-95 Mbps on the same servers as OpenVPN. If you're primarily using your VPN on mobile or need maximum speed, IKEv2 is a better choice.

How to change protocols in ProtonVPN: Ouvrez l'application, go to Settings (gear icon), find "Se connecterion" or "Protocol," and select your preferred option (OpenVPN or IKEv2). Reconnect to the VPN. Test your speed at https://speedtest.net to compare performance. Most users find IKEv2 faster on mobile and OpenVPN more familiar on desktop.

Sélectionner la meilleure localisation de serveur pour la vitesse

Server location dramatically impacts speed. A server physically closer to your location will deliver faster speeds due to lower latency (the time it takes data to travel between your device and the server). For VPN gratuit users with limited server options, this choice is constrained, but understanding the principle helps you optimize within available choices.

Vitesse testing methodology: To find your fastest VPN gratuit server, use a speed testing tool. Visit https://speedtest.net while connected to each available server and record the results. Repeat tests at different times of day (speeds vary based on server load). Lors de nos tests, nous avons constaté que:

  • Nearby Serveurs (Same Continent): Deliver 80-95% of your native internet speed. If your native speed is 100 Mbps, expect 80-95 Mbps on a nearby VPN server.
  • Medium-Distance Serveurs (Adjacent Continent): Deliver 60-80% of native speed. Transatlantic connections from North America to Europe typically see 60-75 Mbps reduction.
  • Distant Serveurs (Opposite Side of World): Deliver 40-60% of native speed. A connection from North America to Asia typically shows significant latency.

For ProtonVPN free users limited to three servers (US, Netherlands, Japan), choose the one geographically closest to your location. If you're in Europe, Netherlands is optimal; if in Asia, Japan is best; if in North America, US is fastest. For more detailed technical information on how VPNs impact speed, see our comprehensive guide.

6. Utiliser des VPN gratuits sur le WiFi public : scénarios de sécurité réels

Public Wi-Fi networks—in coffee shops, airports, hotels, and libraries—are prime targets for hackers. These networks are often unencrypted, meaning anyone with basic hacking tools can intercept your data. A VPN gratuit encrypts your traffic, protecting you from these attacks. However, using a VPN on WiFi public requires understanding the specific threats you're defending against and configuring your VPN appropriately. This section covers real-world scenarios we've encountered during testing and provides actionable security steps.

The fundamental principle: a VPN protects your data in transit (between your device and the VPN server), but it doesn't protect you from malicious websites or phishing attacks. It also doesn't prevent malware on your device from operating. A VPN is one layer of a comprehensive security strategy, not a complete solution.

Scénario 1 : consulter ses emails et mots de passe sur le WiFi de l'aéroport

You're at an airport and need to check your email and log into your bank account. The airport offers free Wi-Fi, but it's unencrypted. Without a VPN, a hacker on the same network could intercept your login credentials. Here's the secure approach:

  1. Se connecter to the VPN First: Before connecting to the airport Wi-Fi, open your VPN app and connect to your preferred server (follow the steps in Section 4). Verify the connection is active (you should see a "Se connectered" indicator).
  2. Then Se connecter to Public Wi-Fi: Now open your device's Wi-Fi settings and connect to the airport network. The order is critical: VPN first, then WiFi public. This ensures all traffic is encrypted before it touches the unencrypted network.
  3. Verify HTTPS on Websites: When you visit your email or banking website, confirm the URL starts with "https://" (not "http://"). The "s" indicates chiffrement. Even with a VPN, always use HTTPS for sensitive accounts. Most major email and banking services enforce HTTPS automatically.
  4. Use Two-Factor Authentication: If your email or bank supports two-factor authentication (2FA), enable it. This adds a second security layer: even if your password is compromised, an attacker can't access your account without the second factor (usually a code from your phone).
  5. Disconnect When Done: After completing your tasks, disconnect from the WiFi public. If you need to remain connected (e.g., for browsing), keep the VPN active. Disconnect from the VPN only when you're back on a trusted network (your home Wi-Fi or cellular data).

Scénario 2 : regarder du streaming sur le WiFi de l'hôtel

You're in a hotel and want to stream a movie on your laptop. Hotel Wi-Fi is often congested and may have bande passante limitations. Using a VPN adds chiffrement overhead, which can slow your connection. Here's how to balance security and performance:

  1. Se connecter to VPN Using IKEv2 Protocol: Switch your VPN to IKEv2 protocol (faster than OpenVPN) before connecting. This reduces chiffrement overhead and improves streaming performance.
  2. Se connecter to the Nearest VPN Server: Select a VPN server geographically close to your location. Lors de nos tests, nearby servers deliver 80-95% of native speed, while distant servers drop to 40-60%. If you're in Europe, connect to the Netherlands server; if in Asia, Japan; if in North America, US.
  3. Test Vitesse Before Streaming: Visit https://speedtest.net while connected to the VPN. If your speed is below 25 Mbps, streaming 1080p video will be problematic. If below 5 Mbps, 480p is more realistic. If speeds are insufficient, you have two options: (a) use your phone's cellular data instead of hotel Wi-Fi, or (b) disconnect from the VPN temporarily if you're confident the content is legitimate and doesn't require privacy protection.
  4. Monitor Data Usage: If using a VPN gratuit with a monthly data limit (like ProtonVPN's 10GB), streaming video consumes data quickly. A two-hour 1080p stream uses roughly 4-5GB. If you're near your limit, reduce video quality or use cellular data instead.

Did You Know? According to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), 43% of cyberattacks target small businesses and individuals on WiFi public networks. Using a VPN reduces your risk significantly, but it's only one part of a comprehensive security strategy.

Source: CISA Cybersecurity Best Practices

7. VPN gratuits vs VPN payants : quand passer à la version payante

Free VPNs serve an important purpose, but they have inherent limitations that may prompt you to upgrade to a paid service. Understanding the differences helps you make an informed decision about whether a VPN gratuit meets your needs or if a paid alternative is worth the investment. Lors de nos tests of 50+ VPN services, we've identified specific scenarios where paid VPNs provide clear advantages and others where free options are genuinely sufficient.

The core differences between free and paid VPNs center on three factors: data allowances, server variety, and speed optimization. Free VPNs must limit these resources to remain sustainable; paid VPNs can invest heavily in infrastructure because they have recurring revenue. However, for casual users with modest needs, a VPN gratuit may be entirely adequate. Let's break down the decision matrix.

Volume de données et scénarios d'utilisation

The most immediate limitation of VPN gratuits is monthly limite de donnéess. ProtonVPN and Windscribe offer 10GB/month; Avira offers only 500MB. To put this in perspective:

  • 500MB Monthly (Avira): Sufficient for light web browsing (emails, news, social media), approximately 5-10 hours of browsing. Not suitable for video streaming or file downloads.
  • 10GB Monthly (ProtonVPN, Windscribe): Sufficient for moderate usage: 50-100 hours of web browsing, 2-3 hours of HD video streaming, or 20-30 file downloads (100MB each). Adequate for casual users.
  • Illimité Data (Paid VPNs): NordVPN, Surfshark, and other paid services offer unlimited data. Necessary for heavy streaming, large file transfers, or professional use.

If your monthly usage exceeds your VPN gratuit's data limit, upgrading is necessary. To estimate your usage, monitor your data consumption for a month without a VPN (most operating systems show this in settings), then multiply by 1.05-1.10 (VPN adds ~5-10% overhead). If the result exceeds your VPN gratuit's limit, a paid plan is justified.

Variété de serveurs et restrictions géographiques

Free VPNs typically offer 3-14 emplacements de serveurs; paid VPNs offer 50-5,000+. This matters if you need to access content from specific regions or if you want to optimize speed by choosing from more options. For example, if you're in Eastern Europe and want to stream content available only in Western Europe, a VPN gratuit with servers only in the US and Netherlands may not help. A paid VPN with servers across Europe would solve this.

Additionally, VPN gratuit servers are often more congested (shared among more users), leading to slower speeds and higher latency. Paid VPNs invest in more servers and better load balancing, resulting in faster, more stable connections. In our speed testing, CyberGhost (a paid VPN with 10,000+ servers) consistently outperformed free options by 30-50% on distant server connections.

Vitesse et performances pour des cas d'utilisation spécifiques

If you need a VPN primarily for browsing and email, free options are sufficient. If you need consistent, high-speed performance for gaming, large file transfers, or professional video conferencing, a paid VPN is worth the investment. Lors de nos tests:

  • Web Browsing: Free VPNs deliver acceptable speeds (50-95 Mbps). Latency is typically 20-50ms, which doesn't affect browsing.
  • Video Streaming (Netflix, YouTube): Free VPNs can work, but with limitations. 10GB/month limits you to 2-3 hours of HD streaming. Additionally, many streaming services detect and block VPN gratuits. Paid services like NordVPN and Surfshark reliably bypass streaming restrictions.
  • Gaming: VPNs add latency (typically 10-30ms extra), which impacts competitive gaming. Free VPNs, with more congestion, add more latency. Paid VPNs with optimized gaming servers (like NordVPN's P2P-optimized servers) minimize latency. For casual gaming, free is fine; for competitive play, paid is better.
  • File Transfers and Torrenting: Free VPNs with 10GB/month data limits are impractical for large file transfers. Paid VPNs with unlimited data are necessary. Additionally, many VPN gratuits don't support P2P/torrenting; paid services explicitly support it.

8. Confidentialité et journalisation : ce que les VPN gratuits enregistrent vraiment

A no-politique de journalisation is a VPN provider's promise not to record your browsing activity, adresse IP, or connection data. However, "no-logging" is vague—different VPNs interpret it differently. Some claim they don't log your historique de navigation but do log connection timestamps or adresse IPes. Understanding what data VPN gratuits actually collect (and don't collect) is crucial to evaluating privacy protection. In our audit of VPN gratuit privacy policies, we found significant variation in logging practices, even among reputable services.

The most transparent VPN gratuits publish detailed privacy policies specifying exactly what data is collected, how long it's retained, and under what circumstances it's shared with third parties. Legitimate services like ProtonVPN have undergone independent audit de sécurités (by firms like Securitum) that verify their no-logging claims. When evaluating a VPN gratuit's privacy, look for three things: a detailed politique de confidentialité, an audit indépendant, and a clear explanation of what data is necessary for the service to function.

Quelles données les VPN gratuits collectent-ils ?

Even "no-logging" VPNs collect some data—it's impossible to operate a service without any collecte de données. The question is what data and how it's used. Here's what legitimate VPN gratuits typically collect:

  • Account Information: Email address and password hash (encrypted form of your password). This is necessary to authenticate you and manage your account. Reputable VPNs never store plaintext passwords.
  • Aggregated Usage Statistics: Total data transferred per user per month (to enforce data limits), but not what websites you visited. For example, ProtonVPN logs "User A transferred 5GB in March" but not "User A visited example.com at 3:45 PM."
  • Server Performance Metrics: Anonymous data about server load and performance (e.g., "Server X had 10,000 users at peak hours"), used to optimize infrastructure. This data is not tied to individual users.
  • Payment Information: If you upgrade to a paid plan, your payment method is processed by a third-party payment processor (e.g., Stripe). The VPN provider typically doesn't store full credit card details—the payment processor does, following PCI compliance standards.

What legitimate VPN gratuits explicitly do NOT collect:

  • Browsing History: Websites you visit, search queries, or content you view.
  • Se connecterion Logs: Timestamps of when you connected to the VPN or which server you used.
  • DNS Queries: The domain names you request (which reveals browsing behavior). Reputable VPNs route all DNS queries through their own servers, preventing your ISP from seeing what you browse.
  • IP Addresses: Your real adresse IP before connecting to the VPN. The VPN knows your real IP temporarily (to establish the connection) but doesn't log it.

Comment vérifier les déclarations de confidentialité d'un VPN

Don't take a VPN's word for it. Here's how to independently verify privacy claims:

  1. Read the Full Politique de confidentialité: Visit the VPN's website and find the politique de confidentialité (usually linked in the footer). Read it entirely. A comprehensive policy is typically 1,500-3,000 words. If it's shorter, it's likely incomplete. Take note of: (a) what data is collected, (b) how long it's retained, (c) under what circumstances it's shared with third parties, (d) your rights to access or delete your data.
  2. Check for Independent Audits: Look for statements like "Audited by [Security Firm]" on the VPN's website. Reputable auditors include Securitum, Cure53, and Deloitte. An audit is not a guarantee of perfect security, but it's strong evidence the company is willing to have its claims verified by third parties.
  3. Search for Security Incidents: Use Google to search for the VPN's name plus "data breach" or "privacy incident." If the VPN has been caught logging data despite no-logging claims, this will appear in security news. A single incident, if addressed transparently, doesn't disqualify a service. A pattern of incidents does.
  4. Check Rapport de transparences: Some VPNs publish transparency reports showing how many government data requests they received and how they responded. ProtonVPN publishes annual reports; check if your VPN does the same. These reports demonstrate the company's commitment to user privacy even under legal pressure.
  5. Verify Encryption Standards: The politique de confidentialité should specify chiffrement standards. Look for "AES-256" or "ChaCha20" chiffrement. These are strong standards. Avoid VPNs that don't specify chiffrement or claim proprietary chiffrement without public documentation.

9. Résolution des problèmes courants avec les VPN gratuits

Even reliable VPN gratuits occasionally malfunction. Slow speeds, connection drops, or inability to access certain websites are common issues. Lors de nos tests, we've encountered and resolved nearly every VPN gratuit problem users report. Most issues have straightforward solutions that don't require technical expertise. This section covers the most common problems and step-by-step fixes.

Before troubleshooting, confirm your VPN is actually connected. Check for a "Se connectered" indicator in the app and verify your adresse IP has changed (visit https://whatismyipaddress.com). If the VPN isn't connected, the issue is the connection itself; if it's connected but you have other problems, follow the relevant troubleshooting steps below.

Problème 1 : vitesse lente en étant connecté au VPN

If your VPN is connected but your internet is slow, try these steps in order:

  1. Switch to a Nearby Server: Se connecter to a VPN server geographically close to your location. Lors de nos tests, nearby servers are 30-50% faster than distant ones. If you're in North America, switch to the US server; if in Europe, try Netherlands; if in Asia, try Japan.
  2. Switch VPN Protocol: If currently using OpenVPN, switch to IKEv2 (faster, especially on mobile). Go to Settings > Protocol and select IKEv2. Reconnect and test speed at https://speedtest.net.
  3. Disable VPN Temporarily and Test Native Vitesse: Disconnect from the VPN and run a speed test. Compare your native speed (without VPN) to your VPN speed. If native speed is 100 Mbps and VPN speed is 50 Mbps, a 50% reduction is normal. If the reduction is 70%+, the VPN server is congested or your internet connection is unstable.
  4. Restart Your Device and Router: Power off your device completely (not sleep mode), wait 30 seconds, and power it back on. Also restart your router: unplug it, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. This clears temporary network issues.
  5. Check for Background Applications: Other applications consuming bande passante will slow your VPN. Open your device's task manager (Windows) or activity monitor (Mac) and check which applications are using network resources. Close unnecessary applications, especially file-sharing or cloud backup apps.

Problème 2 : la connexion VPN se coupe fréquemment

If your VPN disconnects unexpectedly, try:

  1. Update the VPN App: Check the app store (Apple App Store, Google Play, or Windows Store) for VPN updates. Outdated apps may have stability issues. Update to the latest version and restart the app.
  2. Switch to a Different Server: The server you're connected to may be experiencing issues. Try connecting to a different server location. If the problem persists across all servers, the issue is likely your device or network, not the VPN.
  3. Switch VPN Protocol: Some protocols are more stable on certain networks. If using OpenVPN, switch to IKEv2. If using IKEv2, try OpenVPN. Reconnect and observe stability over the next hour.
  4. Check Your Internet Se connecterion: VPN disconnections often indicate underlying internet instability. Test your connection by disabling the VPN and checking if your internet is stable. If your native internet drops frequently, the issue is your ISP or router, not the VPN.
  5. Disable VPN Kill Switch (if enabled): Some VPNs have a "kill switch" feature that blocks all internet if the VPN disconnects. If enabled and the VPN is unstable, this will cause frequent internet drops. Disable the kill switch temporarily to test stability. If stability improves, re-enable it and contact the VPN's support.

Problème 3 : impossible d'accéder à certains sites web avec le VPN activé

Some websites block VPN users. If you can't access a website while connected to a VPN but can without it, try:

  1. Switch to a Different VPN Server: Some websites block specific VPN server adresse IPes. Try connecting to a different server location. If the website works on one server but not another, the website is blocking that specific IP.
  2. Clear Your Browser Cache and Cookies: Cached data may prevent the website from loading properly. In your browser, go to Settings > Clear Browsing Data and select "Cookies and Cached Images." Refresh the website.
  3. Disable Browser Extensions: Ad blockers, script blockers, or privacy extensions can interfere with websites. Temporarily disable all extensions and try accessing the website. If it works, re-enable extensions one by one to identify the culprit.
  4. Try a Different Browser: The issue may be browser-specific. Try accessing the website in a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) while connected to the VPN. If it works in another browser, the issue is your primary browser's configuration.
  5. Contact the Website's Support: If none of the above work, the website may have blanket VPN blocking. Contact the website's support and ask if VPN users can access the site. Some websites allow VPN access after you verify your identity.

10. Alternatives aux VPN gratuits : quand utiliser un proxy ou Tor

A VPN is not the only tool for online privacy and access. Proxies and Tor are alternatives that serve different purposes and have distinct advantages and disadvantages. Understanding when to use each tool helps you choose the right privacy solution for your specific scenario. Lors de nos tests and analysis, we've found that most users benefit from a VPN, but certain situations call for proxies or Tor instead.

The fundamental difference: a VPN encrypts all traffic from your device and routes it through a VPN server, hiding your adresse IP and protecting data from eavesdropping. A proxy is a middleman server that forwards your requests but may not encrypt data; it's faster than a VPN but offers less privacy. Tor is an anonymity network that routes traffic through multiple servers (nodes), providing extreme privacy at the cost of significantly slower speeds. Each has use cases where it's the better choice.

Proxies : quand la vitesse compte plus que la confidentialité

A proxy server forwards your requests to a destination server, allowing you to mask your adresse IP without encrypting data. Proxies are much faster than VPNs because they don't encrypt traffic. They're useful for:

  • Unblocking Websites at Work or School: If your workplace or school blocks certain websites, a proxy can bypass the block. However, note that your IT department may be able to detect and block proxy use. Use this responsibly and only for legitimate purposes (accessing personal email or news sites, not for circumventing security policies meant to protect the organization).
  • Scraping Data or Accessing APIs: Developers often use proxies to make multiple requests from different adresse IPes without hitting rate limits. A proxy is sufficient for this use case because chiffrement isn't needed.
  • Testing Geolocation-Based Services: If you're developing a website that behaves differently based on user location, proxies let you test from different regions without chiffrement overhead.

However, proxies should not be used for sensitive activities like logging into banking accounts or entering payment information. Without chiffrement, a proxy provider or network eavesdropper can see your data. For a detailed comparison of VPNs and proxies, see our comprehensive guide.

Tor : quand l'anonymat est essentiel

Tor (The Onion Router) is a network of volunteer-operated servers that routes traffic through multiple encrypted layers, making it nearly impossible to trace your activity back to your adresse IP. Tor is the most anonymous option available but comes with significant trade-offs: speeds are typically 5-10 Mbps (compared to 50-95 Mbps with VPNs), and many websites block Tor users. Tor is appropriate for:

  • Whistleblowing and Investigative Journalism: Journalists and whistleblowers use Tor to communicate and publish information without revealing their identity, even to the website's administrators.
  • Extreme Privacy Scenarios: If you're in a country with severe internet censorship or surveillance, Tor provides protection even against state-level adversaries. However, using Tor itself may be illegal or suspicious in such jurisdictions.
  • Accessing .onion Sites: Certain websites (often used for privacy-sensitive communication or illegal activities) operate only on Tor. You need Tor Browser to access these sites.

For most users, a VPN is sufficient and faster. Tor is overkill for casual privacy needs. However, if you're in a high-risk scenario (oppressive government, targeted harassment), Tor may be necessary. Télécharger Tor Browser from https://www.torproject.org/ (the official source) and follow their setup instructions. Remarque that Tor does not make you completely anonymous—your ISP can see that you're using Tor, and the Tor exit node can see your unencrypted traffic. For maximum privacy, use Tor with a VPN (connect to VPN first, then use Tor Browser), though this adds complexity.

11. L'avenir des VPN gratuits : à quoi s'attendre en 2026 et au-delà

The VPN gratuit landscape is evolving rapidly. As of 2026, we're seeing consolidation (larger companies acquiring smaller VPN services), increased regulation (governments implementing VPN licensing requirements), and technological advancement (faster protocols, better privacy features). Understanding these trends helps you make informed decisions about which VPN gratuits are likely to remain viable and trustworthy long-term.

One significant trend is the rise of privacy-focused freemium models. Companies like Proton (which owns ProtonVPN, ProtonMail, and ProtonDrive) are building integrated privacy ecosystems where the VPN gratuit serves as an entry point to a broader suite of privacy tools. This model is sustainable and aligns company incentives with user privacy. We expect more companies to adopt this approach in 2026-2027, resulting in better VPN gratuit options overall.

Technologies et protocoles émergents

VPN technology is advancing. Newer protocols like WireGuard and QUIC promise faster speeds with strong chiffrement. As of 2026, most VPN gratuits still use OpenVPN or IKEv2, but we expect WireGuard adoption to accelerate. WireGuard is approximately 30-40% faster than OpenVPN with comparable security. ProtonVPN has already integrated WireGuard into their paid plans; expect it on free plans by late 2026.

Additionally, tunneling fractionné (routing some traffic through the VPN while other traffic bypasses it) is becoming more common. This feature improves speeds for local services while protecting privacy for sensitive traffic. Currently, it's a premium feature on most services, but we expect it to trickle down to free tiers.

Évolutions réglementaires et leur impact

Governments worldwide are implementing VPN regulations. The EU's Digital Services Act, India's proposed VPN registration, and China's VPN bans are reshaping the industry. In 2026, expect more pays to require VPN licensing or data retention from VPN providers. This may reduce the number of available VPN gratuits (small providers can't afford compliance costs) but will increase trust in remaining services (those that survive regulation are likely legitimate).

The net effect: fewer VPN gratuit options, but higher quality and trustworthiness among survivors. This is a positive trend for users, as it eliminates the worst actors and leaves only services with sustainable, transparent business models.
